title: Rampnotes: LLM deployment playbook + paper links
content:
Quick context: stash of short summaries and tactical experiments to run on staging Redwood clusters. This is a living scratchpad — mostly for my own ramp-up and to hand off to Aisha/Samir when we spin a short spike.

High-level goals
- Understand which paper-level trick gives the best latency/cost uplift for our medium-tail production prompts (avg length ~ 120 tokens, 99th ~ 600 tokens).
- Prioritize changes that are safe for Hosted API first (non-breaking), then evaluate Dedicated/Private rollout.
- Produce a one-page ops checklist for the next oncall and a lightweight benchmark runbook.

Paper summaries / takeaways (very short)
1) "Prefix KV caching and selective retention" (recent conf talk notes) - idea: keep dense prefixes in fast NVMe cache and evict older minutes-based entries; selective retention based on token reuse score.
   - takeaway: for chat-like workloads with repeated context, prefix caching gives big p95 wins; eviction policy matters a lot.
   - ops note: test with our existing per-user short-term cache + TTL=600s vs scoring-based retention.
   - link: arXiv-ish notes in linked_artifacts.

2) "Dynamic quantization knobs for throughput-sensitive lanes" (paper A)
   - takeaway: use mixed precision per-layer; quantize attention + MLP differently. Latency slightly better, but some prompt-dependent quality changes.
   - ops note: add a quick A/B to Redwood Optimize recommendations to flag risky quant profiles when eval set fails similarity threshold.

3) "Shard-first KV cache for long context" (paper B)
   - takeaway: shard by prefix hash to keep per-GPU KV size bounded — reduces memory blowouts. Worth combination with partial caching (only last N tokens per shard).
   - ops risk: fallback behaviour when a shard is missed must be predictable (latency tail).

Conference takeaways (from notes)
- People are pushing hybrid: partial attention + sparse retrieval for longer contexts rather than full 64k sequences all the time. Operationally easier to restrict to 16k + retrieval.
- Benchmarks are noisy — gotta standardize prompt families.

Experiments to prioritize (short-run + measurable)
1) Cache eviction policy sweep (staging):
   - compare TTL(300/600/1800), LRU, and score-based retention on a 48-hour replay of prod traffic (sample).
   - metrics: p50/p95 latency, token cost (GPU cycles), quality delta (BLEU-like or embedding-sim).
   - acceptance: >15% p95 reduction with <=1% quality drop.

2) KV shard size cap (staging/dedicated):
   - implement soft cap per-GPU + spill-to-SSD fallback (measure tail).
   - observe memory OOM events reduction and tail latency tradeoffs.

3) Quantization A/B: select 3 quant profiles (safe, aggressive, layer-adaptive) and run on a small user cohort in Hosted (low traffic)
   - collect hallucination/regression signals via existing eval harness.

Notes for Redwood-specific integration
- Serving-runtime: kernel selection needs to be stable across mixed-quant runs; ensure we pin kernel sets in the staging image.
- Smart routing: for test cohorts, route to Dedicated lanes when we want strict latency SLOs and keep Hosted for broad experiments.
- Observability: add a short-lived dashboard tile for "cache-miss-induced latency" and a tag on traces that miss shard vs hit shard.

Open questions / unknowns
- How cost-effective is NVMe-backed spill vs more aggressive eviction? (need a regression cost model)
- For quantization, can we automatically detect prompt classes that are fragile and route them to higher-precision lanes? (policy complexity vs benefit?)
- How do fallbacks interact with multi-tenant Dedicated pools — if fallback goes to Hosted, do we surface that to customers? SLA implications.

Practical checklist for next spike
- [ ] prepare 48h sampled traffic replay (Samir)
- [ ] implement TTL/score-based eviction variant (Aisha + infra)
- [ ] add trace tag for shard-hit/shard-miss (meera)
- [ ] baseline run for current p50/p95 on staging (bench script: bench/cache-replay-v1)
- [ ] short doc summarizing results and recommended default (1 page)

Hand-off notes (for Aisha/Samir)
- If you pick this up: start with the cache evictions sweep. I pushed a tiny harness to github: linked_artifacts above. Keep configs simple and record exact config IDs.
- Use the "eval prompt family" set from /confluence/rapid-evals (linked in Confluence) for quality checks.

Random reminders to self
- Keep test cohorts small and tagged so billing is contained.
- Don't merge kernel-level optimizations to hosted images until we validate on Dedicated nodes (fallback blast radius).

End of rampnotes — intended to be concise and actionable. Will expand into a proper spec if an experiment looks promising.
